t: You're looking at St Alfege Church in Greenwich. Of medieval origin, it reputedly marks the spot where Alfege, Archbishop of Canterbury, was martyred in 1012. The building you see went up between 1712 and 1714, designed by Nicholas Hawksmoor after the old church collapsed. Hawksmoor was a leading figure of English Baroque who also worked on Greenwich Hospital. Several musicians are buried here, including the great Renaissance composer Thomas Tallis and Nicholas Lanier, the first Master of the King's Music. General James Wolfe, who won at Quebec in 1759, is buried here too.
